units.topics: Study of the human head including planes, depth, raised portions, and facial construction through analytical drawing methods.

units.title: Ancient Indian Wall Paintings
units.topics: Study of the evolution, stylistic features, architectural context, and artists of Indian mural traditions with reference to:  Ajanta (200 B.C.–200 A.D. & 4th–6th Century A.D.)  Bagh (5th–6th Century A.D.)  Badami (c. 578 A.D.)  Ellora (750–800 A.D.)  Sittanavasal (9th Century A.D.)  Tanjavur (10th–11th Century A.D.)

units.title: Jain and Pala Miniature Paintings
units.topics: Study of manuscript painting traditions including stylistic development, themes, symbolism, and techniques in: • Jain Kalpa Sūtra Manuscripts • Kālakācārya-kathā • Vasant Vilas (1450) with emphasis on painting evolution and manuscript illustration practices.

units.title: Mughal School of Painting
units.topics: Critical study of the development of Mughal painting under royal patronage during the reigns of:  Humayun  Akbar  Jahangir  Shah Jahan focusing on Persian influence, naturalism, portraiture, court scenes, and artists’ contributions.

units.title: Rajput School of Painting
units.topics: Study of the stylistic diversity, regional characteristics, themes, and architectural influence in Rajput painting traditions including:  Bundi  Basohli  Kishangarh  Kotah

units.title: Pahari School of Painting
units.topics: Study of Guler and Kangra schools with special reference to lyrical expression, romantic themes, color schemes, and contribution of artists in the evolution of Indian miniature painting.

units.topics: Study of aesthetic theories of Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle with reference to beauty, imitation (Mimesis), and art criticism.

units.title: Baroque Art and Architecture
units.topics: Study of the dramatic style, movement, light effects, realism, and architectural innovations in Baroque art with reference to major artists and architects such as Bernini, Borromini, Caravaggio, Rubens, Rembrandt, Vermeer, Velázquez, Frans Hals, Rosa, and Nicolas Poussin.

units.title: Rococo and Neoclassical Art Movements
units.topics: Examination of the decorative elegance of Rococo art and the revival of classical ideals in Neoclassicism through the works of Watteau, François Boucher, Hogarth, Reynolds, Gainsborough, Jacques-Louis David, and Ingres.

units.title: Romanticism and Realism
units.topics: Study of emotional expression, imagination, nationalism, and social realities in Romantic and Realist art through the works of Géricault, Delacroix, Turner, Constable, Goya, Courbet, Millet, Daumier, Thomas Eakins, and Andrew Wyeth.

units.title: Impressionism
units.topics: Exploration of modern approaches to light, color, atmosphere, and everyday life in Impressionist painting with special reference to Manet, Monet, Renoir, Degas, and Mary Cassatt.

units.title: Post-Impressionism and Modern Artistic Expression
units.topics: Study of individual artistic experimentation, structure, symbolism, and expressive use of color in the works of Cézanne, Van Gogh, Gauguin, Seurat, and Henri Rousseau, leading toward modern art movements.

units.title: Modern Western Aesthetic Theories
units.topics: Study of aesthetic ideas of Kant, Hegel, Croce, and Tolstoy with emphasis on beauty, expression, and art as experience.

units.title: Formalism and Expressionism in Art
units.topics: Concepts of form, design, emotional expression, symbolism, and abstraction in modern art movements.

units.title: Art Criticism and Contemporary Aesthetic Thought
